Why nothing was un-flagged

the index charges  len(name) + len(description)
a FLAGGED skill contributes 0, so un-flagging adds its FULL cost
with nothing of its own to trim against

  headroom                     34 bytes
  cheapest candidate  langgraph  9 name  ──▶  25 bytes for a description
                                             not reachable

The substantive reason holds regardless of budget. Every remaining target is a ROUTER skill: SKILL.md is a table of contents and the substance lives in rules/ and references/. A preload delivers SKILL.md only, so un-flagging monitoring-observability would spend permanent per-session tokens to hand an agent a contents page and none of the Langfuse v4 API surface it wanted. It fails on delivery before it fails on budget.

The third answer: convert, do not delete

- skills:
-   - monitoring-observability      # never resolved

+ ## Domain Reference
+
+ The `monitoring-observability` skill is slash-only, so it cannot be
+ preloaded. Load it explicitly when you need its rules and references:
+ `Read("${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/monitoring-observability/SKILL.md")`.

Not invented here. Read("${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/shared/status-protocol.md") already appears in 35 of 36 agent bodies, and genui-architect already points at skill files the same way. Agent BODIES are in no token budget, so all 9 conversions cost nothing against any cap. A pointer also reaches rules/ and references/, which a preload never would.

A test caught a delete that was wrong

tests/agents/test-frontend-performance-engineer.sh asserts that agent carries monitoring-observability and vite-advanced. Deleting them turned it red. The agent's own description says it "sets up RUM", so a human had encoded a real requirement and the delete recommendation missed it. Both were promoted to Read pointers instead of weakening the test.

And the test itself has the same blind spot
It greps the WHOLE FILE for the skill name. vite-advanced kept passing after its frontmatter entry was deleted, because the string still appeared in a prose line at :269. A false pass, from the same family as the linter that reported DEAD-EDGE: 0. Flagged, not silently rewritten.
